notes: Neighbourhood inferred from the name; confirm.
blurb: A conservative family Puja at 78 Nimtala Ghat Street, Hatkhola, in a house that is over 200 years old.
dishes: Nilkantha bird ritual to close the Puja

tips.expect: A traditional, old-Calcutta household Puja rather than a spectacle, with strict family rituals.
tips.good: The nilkantha (blue jay) ritual at the close of the Puja, when the birds are released to carry the goddess's message to Shiva.
tips.watch: Nimtala Ghat Street leads to the Ganga, so expect traffic restrictions and processions around Dashami.
tips.tip: Visit on Saptami or Ashtami morning for the most relaxed darshan.

blurb: A 170-year-old Puja at 15 Ramnath Kabiraj Lane, started by Rashmoni Dasi, with a rare ashtadhatu idol of Singhabahini.

tips.expect: A smaller, intimate house Puja in the Baghbazar lanes, with a family that also celebrates Kali Puja.
tips.good: The metal idol is unusual for the city, and the stained-glass decoration around the dalan is lovely in the evening.
tips.watch: The lanes are tight and unlit in places, so keep your phone torch handy after dark.
tips.tip: Pair with Baghbazar Sarbojanin, Kumartuli and Nobin Chandra Das for a very compact North Kolkata loop.

blurb: The Seal family's Puja at 42 Muktaram Babu Street, running since about 1855 in the Vaishnav tradition.

tips.expect: A beautifully decorated thakurdalan in a Vaishnav household, so no animal sacrifice and a gentler feel.
tips.good: Chorbagan has several old Puja houses on one street, so it is easy to see a few in a short walk.
tips.watch: Muktaram Babu Street is a busy business street by day, with little room to stand and look.
tips.tip: Combine with Chorbagan Mitra Bari next door and the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal.

blurb: The Mitra family house at 84 Muktaram Babu Street, built by the moneylender Ramsundar Mitra and said to be among the oldest Pujas in the city.
dishes: Gothic entrance with six large pillars

tips.expect: A grand old house with a Gothic-style pillared entrance that was renovated by Macintosh & Burn, and a long-running Durga and Kali Puja.
tips.good: The architecture is as much the draw as the Puja.
tips.watch: Claims of 300+ years are family tradition and I could not confirm them independently.
tips.tip: Good for a morning or afternoon visit when the street is quiet.

blurb: Dwarakanath Dutta started this Vaishnav-style Puja at 3 Bidhan Sarani in 1855. He is remembered for giving workers a Puja bonus.

tips.expect: A calm, traditional household Puja just off the Thanthania Kalibari, with no animal sacrifice.
tips.good: It is easy to reach and rarely packed, so you can take your time.
tips.watch: Bidhan Sarani itself is a very busy road, so cross carefully.
tips.tip: Pair it with a stop at Thanthania Kalibari and College Street for coffee.

blurb: The Roy family's Colootola Puja at 2A Gopal Chandra Lane, running since 1858 in a Vaishnav household that uses fruit for the symbolic sacrifice.
dishes: Arched thakur dalan with lamp-topped pillars

tips.expect: A handsome arched thakur dalan around a quadrangle, with side lighting that makes it glow at night. The puja moved briefly in 1946 and then returned.
tips.good: One of the prettiest dalans in North Kolkata after dark.
tips.watch: Colootola's lanes are tight, so don't try to bring a car.
tips.tip: Walk here from College Street or Central metro. Also called the Kolutolla Rajbari.

blurb: A Puja of 175 years or more at 4 Thakurdas Palit Lane, with a nicely decorated thakurdalan.

tips.expect: A modest, traditional house Puja in a tight Central Kolkata lane.
tips.good: The decorations around the thakurdalan.
tips.watch: Little is written about this house, so hours and access may differ from year to year.
tips.tip: Combine with Nilmani Mitra Bari and Rani Rashmoni Bari on one walk.

blurb: The Mitra family house at 19 Nilmoni Mitra Street, with a Puja started in 1809 by Radha Krishna Mitra.
dishes: Two nilkantha birds released at the end

tips.expect: A traditional old-Calcutta house Puja.
tips.good: The nilkantha ritual: one bird is sent toward Kailash and one towards the sky over Darjipara.
tips.watch: Google Maps pins this as Nilmani Dey's Thakur Bari, a few km south of Darjipara. It is a separate stop from Darjipara Mitra Bari.
tips.tip: Visit in daylight; the lanes are quiet and dark at night.

blurb: Rani Rashmoni's Janbazar mansion, at 13 Rani Rashmoni Road. The Puja here goes back to 1790 and Ramakrishna is said to have worshipped the goddess here in 1864.

tips.expect: A big 19th-century mansion where each branch of the family runs its own courtyard Puja. Rani Rashmoni also founded the Dakshineswar Kali Temple.
tips.good: The ekchala idol decorated with traditional daker saj, and how close it is to Esplanade metro.
tips.watch: Branches in different courtyards mean you may need to ask which entrance (the Free School Street side is one) leads to which Puja.
tips.tip: The easiest Bonedi Bari to add on to a Park Street or New Market evening.

blurb: The Radha Gobinda Mallick family Puja on Mohini Mohan Road, Bhowanipore, moved here in 1925 from an 1860 ancestral home. The family is also known for the film stars Ranjit and Koel Mallick.

tips.expect: South Kolkata's best-known Bonedi Bari, with a bigger crowd than most because of the family's celebrity connection.
tips.good: A real family Puja in the middle of South Kolkata, easy to combine with Bhowanipore food.
tips.watch: Expect queues on Ashtami and Navami evenings. Names like Mullick and Mallick are common, so check the address (Mohini Mohan Road).
tips.tip: Go on Saptami or Dashami for a thinner crowd.

blurb: The Sabarna Roy Choudhury family's Atchala Puja at 26 Sabarna Para Road, Barisha. Started in 1610, it is often called the oldest Durga Puja in the city.

tips.expect: A very old family Puja in Barisha, in the south-west. The Roy Choudhurys were the zamindars of the three villages that became Calcutta.
tips.good: The Atchala dalan and the sense of history. The original structure is still used to prepare the idol.
tips.watch: It is far from the other Baris, so don't try to fit it between two North Kolkata stops. The family runs pujas at several sites.
tips.tip: Give Behala its own half-day. Purple Line stations like Behala Chowrasta are the closest metro.

tips.expect: A Roy family house in Behala. I couldn't find reliable details.
tips.watch: It may be one of the Sabarna Roy Choudhury family's branch pujas in the Barisha area. Confirm before you go.
tips.tip: Visit it with the Atchala Bari in one Behala trip.

blurb: One of the two Deb mansions on Raja Nabakrishna Street. Nabakrishna Deb started the family Puja here in 1757 and famously hosted Robert Clive.

tips.expect: A large mansion with a pillared courtyard and a grand thakurdalan. This is the best known of all the Bonedi Baris, so it draws sightseers as well as devotees.
tips.good: The setting itself: the Natmandir, the lion gate, and the sense of being inside the Puja that shaped the city's Puja tradition.
tips.watch: Queues and foot traffic build up on Ashtami and Navami evenings, and the lanes around Raja Nabakrishna Street are narrow.
tips.tip: Go in the morning or early afternoon for a calm look. It is a short walk from Shobhabazar Sutanuti metro, so skip the car.

blurb: The second Shobhabazar Rajbari, at 33 and 36 Raja Nabakrishna Street. The Deb family's Puja here dates to 1757.
dishes: A lion with a horse's face
Singi fish offered in place of goats (family legend)

tips.expect: Heritage architecture and a family Puja that is also a bit of a museum of old Calcutta. The two Shobhabazar houses stand close together, so you can see both in one go.
tips.good: The unusual lion with a horse's face, and the story behind the family's Clive-era Puja.
tips.watch: Rules at private houses vary: ask before photographing the idol or rituals.
tips.tip: Combine with the thakur dalan and Darjipara and Chatu Babu Latu Babu houses on foot.

blurb: The thakurdalan of the Shobhabazar Rajbari, the heart of the Deb family Puja since 1757.

tips.expect: The main worship hall, with the idol under the pillared arches of the courtyard.
tips.good: Evening lighting makes the arches and columns look their best.
tips.watch: Likely the same compound as the Rajbari entries above, so you may not need to count it as a separate stop.

blurb: Darjipara's Mitra house, a traditional household Puja in the Shobhabazar-Darjipara pocket.

tips.expect: A traditional household Puja in the Darjipara area.
tips.watch: A separate stop from Nilmani Mitra Bari, a few km away.
tips.tip: See the Shobhabazar Rajbaris first, then walk over.

blurb: Ramdulal Nibas at 67E Beadon Street, where Ram Dulal Dey began the Puja in 1770. His sons Asutosh (Chatu Babu) and Pramathanath (Latu Babu) gave the house its name.

tips.expect: A well-known house with a distinctive idol and plenty of visitors.
tips.good: It is on Beadon Street, close to Girish Park metro.
tips.watch: Beadon Street is a busy market road, and the evening crowd is thick.
tips.tip: A good first stop before the Jorasanko and Pathuriaghata houses.

blurb: A Dutta family house at Goa Bagan, Maniktala, bought by Raghunath Dutt in 1922. The idol is of Hara-Parbati and the Puja feels like medieval Bengal.

tips.expect: A traditional, welcoming household Puja. The family serves lunch to more than 400 people every day until Dashami.
tips.good: The unusual Hara-Parbati idol and the community feel. The family is also known for its lantern festival at Kali Puja.
tips.watch: It sits in Maniktala, away from the Girish Park cluster on your list, so it needs its own short detour.
tips.tip: Go around lunchtime to see the community meal.

blurb: A 150-year-old Puja at 122A Maniktala Street, from a family that made its money in the salt trade.
dishes: White house with a big courtyard
White stone lions at the dalan entrance

tips.expect: A white mansion around a large courtyard, with stone lions at the thakurdalan.
tips.good: It photographs well in daylight and is rarely crowded.
tips.watch: Maniktala Main Road is busy, so stick to the footpath.
tips.tip: Combine with Bholanath Dham, Maniktala Chaltabagan and Hatibagan.

tips.expect: A traditional household Puja that starts early, from Krishna Nabami, and keeps up a Kumari Puja on three days. No animal sacrifice.
tips.good: Kumari Puja is the highlight, and the house is a short walk from Girish Park metro.
tips.watch: Balaram De Street is narrow and crowded in the evening.
tips.tip: Pair with the Daw houses and Harakutir for a good heritage walk.

blurb: The Daw family of Jorasanko, who ran the Narasimha Chandra Daw & Co. gun shop from 1835, gave this branch its 'Bandookwala' (gun seller) name.

tips.expect: A Jorasanko family Puja from a family with a business history, close to the Shib Krishna Daw house.
tips.good: Easy to see together with the other Daw house, and close to the Tagore house at Jorasanko.
tips.watch: The Daw family has more than one Puja, so make sure you have the right lane.
tips.tip: Do this and Jorasanko Daw Bari in one go.

blurb: The Daw house at 12A Shibkrishna Daw Lane. The Puja began in 1840 and its thakurdalan has been used for film shoots.

tips.expect: A beautifully kept thakurdalan with balconies around the courtyard, and an idol dressed in heavy gold and silver ornaments.
tips.good: The jewellery and the glittering chalchitra background are what visitors come for.
tips.watch: The Daw family has more than one Puja, so make sure you have the right lane. Daw Bari Bandook Wala is a separate house nearby.
tips.tip: Evening lighting is best for the ornaments.

dishes: Gold and silver ornaments on the goddess

blurb: A 271-year-old house built on what was once a cremation ground beside the Ganga. The family Puja is reported to date back to the late 1690s.

tips.expect: A very old, story-rich house with legends of hidden tunnels used by freedom fighters, and a reported visit by Netaji.
tips.good: The history and atmosphere. You are unlikely to find a crowd.
tips.watch: Details come mainly from family accounts, so treat the dates as tradition.
tips.tip: Ask the family about the tunnel stories if there's a quiet moment.

notes: 47 Pathuriaghata Street. Dhunuchi Nach every evening at approx. 7 pm. Suggested on Saptami.
blurb: The Khelat Ghosh family house at 47 Pathuriaghata Street (Google Maps lists it as Pathuriaghata Rajbari), known for what is often called the grandest thakur dalan in the city, about 80 ft of marble.

tips.expect: A long marble corridor and a grand dancing hall (now the Khelat Ghosh Memorial Hall). Rituals include the ablution of the nine-leaf Naba Patrika at the house. The evening dhunuchi dance is the highlight.
tips.good: The 7 pm dhunuchi nach, then a slow walk through the marble hall. The family also offers homemade sweets to the goddess.
tips.watch: Arrive 20 to 30 minutes early on Saptami to get a decent view.
tips.tip: Plan Pathuriaghata as your last North Kolkata stop so you can stay for the dance.

address: 21B, Hindustan Rd, Ballygunge, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: Amar Khamar Lunch Room at 21B Hindustan Road: an intimate dining room built around seasonal, home-style Bengali cooking.

tips.expect: Seasonal Bengali food sourced from farming communities across Bengal, served in a calm, home-like room. Both fish and meat dishes and vegetarian options are on offer.
tips.good: The Chhuti-r Bhat, a long tasting meal that respects the traditional order of eating.
tips.watch: Reported open Tuesday to Sunday, 12:30 to 10 pm, and closed on Mondays. A full tasting meal takes a while, so don't squeeze it in between pandals.
tips.tip: Go for a slow Puja lunch rather than a rush dinner. It is a short walk from Hindustan Park.

address: 1st Floor, Park Centre, 24, Park St, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700016
blurb: Calcutta's first East-inspired bar and BBQ, on the first floor of Park Centre on Park Street. The menu draws on Japan, Thailand, Vietnam and Singapore.

tips.expect: Alley-dining style Eastern plates and a cocktail programme inspired by informal Japanese drinking culture, from chef Auroni Mookerjee's kitchen.
tips.good: The playful take on local flavours, such as the temaki tacos inspired by prawn cocktail.
tips.watch: It is on the first floor of a commercial building, so the entrance is easy to miss from the street.
tips.tip: A good late-evening stop after Park Street pandal-hopping.

address: 21/7 Aswini Dutta road, Panditiya Rd, beside city style road, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
8B, Maharaj Nanda Kumar Rd, Lake Market, Kalighat, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: A two-floor glasshouse cafe on Lake Road that opened in 2024, mixing old-Calcutta charm with a modern look.
dishes: Shisha and live music in select hours

tips.expect: A large, elegant glass-fronted space with around 120 covers and a global fusion menu.
tips.good: The cold brews and the setting. It is a pleasant place to sit between pandals.
tips.watch: Prices at other outlets are about ₹1,200 for two. Live-music hours are limited.
tips.tip: It sits in the Lake Road cafe cluster, so there are several options within a few minutes if it's full.

address: 12, Ganesh Chandra Ave, Esplanade, Chowringhee North, Bowbazar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700001
blurb: A family-run eating house on Ganesh Chandra Avenue, founded by a Chinese immigrant. It is described as one of the oldest Chinese restaurants in Kolkata, running for 90+ years.

tips.expect: Old-Calcutta Chinese food from family recipes, in a no-frills room.
tips.good: The slow-cooked chimney soup (made in a coal-burning vessel) and the generous portions.
tips.watch: A traditional place that is not about aesthetics. Pork is on the menu, so check if that matters to you.
tips.tip: Combine it with Chinatown and New Market, then walk on to Park Street.

address: Ground Floor, Edward Court, Unit No 11, 1, 55, Chowringee Rd, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071
blurb: A cocktail bar at 1 Edward Court on Chowringhee Road, with old-world decor, weathered walls and a cosy mood.
dishes: The Eavesdropper (tequila, Cointreau, cranberry, Schezwan sauce)

tips.expect: Inventive cocktails and small and big plates with an international twist.
tips.good: The cocktail craft and the unusual food pairings. A strong choice for a date night.
tips.watch: It is a bar first. Puja Saturdays and Sundays will be busy.
tips.tip: Reserve if you can, and note that it is on Chowringhee, far from the North Kolkata circuit.

address: 46A, Prince Gulam Hussain Shah Rd, Jadavpur, Kolkata, West Bengal 700032
GPO Building, Fairley Place, B.B.D. Bagh, Kolkata, West Bengal 700001
blurb: India's first post-office cafe, inside the historic General Post Office at BBD Bagh.

tips.expect: A small cafe with colourful wooden furniture and sofas for about 34 people, inside a colonial building. You can also get parcels packed and buy post-office souvenirs.
tips.good: The setting is the point: coffee under the GPO's arches, away from the crowds.
tips.watch: When it launched it was open 10 am to 7 pm and closed Sundays. Saptami falls on a Sunday this year, so check before you go.
tips.tip: A great weekday morning stop before BBD Bagh and Esplanade sightseeing.

address: 7A, Russel St, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071
blurb: A Park Street tea room at 7A Russel Street serving the Glenburn estate's own Darjeeling, Assam and flavoured teas.

tips.expect: A calm tearoom with small plates and tapas, a break from the Park Street bustle. About ₹800 to ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: The tea list. It is a rare place to try estate teas properly.
tips.watch: Reported hours are 9 am to 9 pm, so it is not a late-night option.
tips.tip: Good for a mid-afternoon reset between Park Street and Esplanade.

address: P, 559, Lake Rd, Hemanta Mukherjee Sarani, lake Terrace, Ballygunge, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: A pizzeria and coffee bar on Lake Road near Southern Avenue, known for wood-fired pizzas and good coffee.

tips.expect: A cosy, welcoming room with friendly service. About ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: The wood-fired char on the pizzas, and the coffee.
tips.watch: Seats go quickly on weekend evenings in the Lake Road and Southern Avenue area.
tips.tip: Combine it with Hindustan Park pandals nearby.

address: 52/A, Paddapukur Rd, Paddapukur, Bhowanipore, Kolkata, West Bengal 700020
blurb: A Parisian-style cafe on Paddapukur Road, Bhowanipore, with chic European decor.

tips.expect: A stylish cafe with an all-day menu of pizza, pasta, Continental, Chinese, desserts and coffee. About ₹1,500 for two.
tips.good: The decor, and a menu broad enough for a mixed group.
tips.watch: It also screens live sports, which can make evenings noisy.
tips.tip: Handy near the Bhowanipore Mallick Bari.

address: 9/10 Jetty, Strand Rd, B.B.D. Bagh, Kolkata, West Bengal 700001
blurb: A garden-inspired vegetarian cafe by the Ganga, on the Polo Floatel at BBD Bagh. It has three zones: Ghar, Verandah and Terrace.

tips.expect: A calm riverside garden vibe with vintage indoor seating, a breezy verandah overlooking the river and a terrace under a gulmohar tree. About ₹800 and up for two.
tips.good: The Ganga view and the all-vegetarian menu, which is unusual for the area.
tips.watch: Open about 11 am to 11 pm. Weekends and evenings fill up for the sunset.
tips.tip: Time it for golden hour, then walk to Esplanade or catch the Strand Road lights.

address: 164, 9/1, Prince Anwar Shah Rd, Jodhpur Gardens, Lake Gardens, Kolkata, West Bengal 700045
blurb: A specialty coffee cafe at Jodhpur Gardens, Lake Gardens, known for Naples-style pizza and good coffee.

tips.expect: An aesthetic cafe with higher prices than a typical coffee shop. About ₹1,200 for two.
tips.good: Quality of coffee and food in a stylish room.
tips.watch: Reported open daily 10 am to 10 pm. Pricey for a casual coffee.
tips.tip: There is another CōLAB at Deshapriya Park, right on the Kalighat pandal route.

address: 8th floor, Shree Lekha Appartment, 42A, Park St, Mullick Bazar, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700016
Y18, Street Number 15, EP Block, Sector V, Bidhannagar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700091
blurb: A Sector V cafe known for playful Indian-fusion plates, open from about noon to 11 pm.

tips.expect: Creative street-food-inspired plates in an easy cafe setting, with outdoor seating. About ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: The Indian-fusion small plates. It is kid-friendly and wheelchair accessible.
tips.watch: There is also a newer vegetarian Milloh on Sarat Bose Road, so check which outlet you mean.
tips.tip: A good stop after Salt Lake pandals, close to Sector V metro.

address: H9XG+XHM, Raja Dinendra Street, Kolkata, near Deshbandhu park, উত্তরেরআড্ডা, West Bengal 700004
49, 1, Golpark, Hindustan Park, Gariahat, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: Sienna Store & Cafe on Hindustan Park, which grew from a home kitchen into a two-storey Bengali-leaning cafe and store.

tips.expect: An artsy, photogenic space with different sections at different price points: a casual cafe, a main dining room and a pricier upscale section. Reported hours are about 11:30 am to 10 pm.
tips.good: Bengali food presented for a modern palate, and the store is nice to browse.
tips.watch: Costs range from roughly ₹500 (cafe) to ₹3,000 (upscale section) for two, so ask which section you're sitting in.
tips.tip: It is steps from the Hindustan Park pandal, so book or go early on busy evenings.

address: 1-3, Wood Burn Rd, Sreepally, Elgin, Kolkata, West Bengal 700020
blurb: Marbella's at 1-3 Woodburn Park Road, Sreepally, a pink-hued, Instagram-friendly cafe.

tips.expect: A stylish cafe with a photogenic menu and decor. About ₹800 to ₹900 for two.
tips.good: Cakes, coffee and aesthetic plates, in a pleasant setting off Elgin Road.
tips.watch: Marbella's has outlets at Elgin and at Hindustan Park, so make sure you choose the right one.
tips.tip: Close to the Bhowanipore Mallick Bari and Elgin Road cafes.

address: 29A, opposite Abin Design Studio, Golpark, Hindustan Park, Gariahat, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: Marbella's Hindustan Park / Golpark outlet, the cafe's busier Gariahat branch.

tips.expect: A pink-hued, photogenic cafe. About ₹800 to ₹900 for two.
tips.good: Sweet treats and coffee, a few steps from Hindustan Park and Sienna.
tips.watch: It is very busy on weekend evenings, especially during Puja.
tips.tip: A good break between Hindustan Park, Maddox Square and Singhi Park.

address: 13A, Sudder St, Fire Brigade Head Quarter, Esplanade, Dharmatala, Taltala, Kolkata, West Bengal 700016
blurb: A colonial bungalow built in 1783 on Sudder Street, a hotel since 1936 and long a favourite of writers, musicians and actors.

tips.expect: A heritage hotel with antique furnishings. Your note on this one says to try the hot chocolate.
tips.good: The old-world setting, in the middle of New Market and Sudder Street.
tips.watch: I couldn't confirm cafe timings or whether non-guests can drop in, so call ahead.
tips.tip: Pair it with the Sudder Street cafes next door and a walk to New Market.

name.en: Craft Coffee Experience Centre - Salt Lake

address: FD-368, FD Block, Sector 3, Bidhannagar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700106
blurb: The Salt Lake FD Block branch of Craft Coffee Experience Centre, a coffee-focused cafe in Sector 3.

tips.expect: A coffee-led cafe with food. Listings put it at roughly ₹1,000 to ₹1,500 for two.
tips.good: Right by the FD Block pandal, so an easy way to rest and refuel during a Salt Lake hop.
tips.watch: Salt Lake gets traffic-heavy at night, so plan the cab back.
tips.tip: Pair with FD Block and Salt Lake's neighbouring blocks.

address: 4, Robinson St, Mullick Bazar, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700017
blurb: An Asian skybar and brewery on Robinson Street, in the Aauris hotel, spread over 6,000 sq ft.

tips.expect: A big, lively bar with three zones: a glasshouse, a semi-outdoor area and open air.
tips.good: The craft beers brewed in-house and the open-air section for a view over Park Street.
tips.watch: Roughly ₹2,000 for two. Puja nights will be packed.
tips.tip: Go for a late drink after the Park Street area pandals.

address: 7, Sudder St, opposite Fire Brigade HQ, Fire Brigade Head Quarter, New Market Area, Dharmatala, Taltala, Kolkata, West Bengal 700016
blurb: A low-key burger spot at 7 Sudder Street. Mark Biswas started it in a garage in 2014 and it grew by word of mouth.

tips.expect: Indulgent burgers in a laid-back, backyard-barbecue mood, tucked away next to Raj's Spanish Cafe.
tips.good: The burgers themselves. This is a cult favourite rather than a big restaurant.
tips.watch: It is small and easy to walk past, so look for it next to Raj's.
tips.tip: A cheap, fast bite when you are near New Market or Park Street.

address: 26, Ballygunge Park Rd, Ballygunge Park, Ballygunge, Kolkata, West Bengal 700019
blurb: Craft Coffee Experience Centre at 26 Ballygunge Park Road, with a high rating among regulars.

tips.expect: A coffee-led cafe with a full menu. About ₹800 to ₹1,500 for two depending on the listing.
tips.good: A good stop on the Ballygunge Cultural and Singhi Park walk.
tips.watch: Seating is limited on busy evenings.
tips.tip: Combine with Ballygunge Cultural Association and Maddox Square.

address: 3Floor, CITI MART, 169, Rash Behari Ave, Ekdalia, Ballygunge, Kolkata, West Bengal 700019
blurb: A pan-Asian restaurant on the third floor of City Mart, 169 Rash Behari Avenue.
dishes: Gai Hor Bai Toey (pandan-wrapped Thai chicken)

tips.expect: A big pan-Asian menu with vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, plus a dance floor and DJ.
tips.good: The dim sum, sushi and Thai steamed chicken. About ₹1,500 for two.
tips.watch: It is on an upper floor of a mall building and can be loud on weekends.
tips.tip: Handy right on the Kalighat and Ballygunge pandal route.

address: 1, Ray St, Sreepally, Bhowanipore, Kolkata, West Bengal 700020
blurb: A specialty coffee roaster at 1 Ray Street, Sreepally, Bhowanipore, with a very high rating.

tips.expect: A relaxed roastery cafe with Italian-leaning food. About ₹1,200 for two.
tips.good: Roasted-in-house coffee, reservations, valet parking and a pet-friendly policy.
tips.watch: It is on the Bhowanipore side, away from the Gariahat cluster.
tips.tip: A good pairing with the Mallick Bari and Elgin Road cafes.

address: Mani Square Mall, 3rd Floor, 164/1 Maniktala Main Road, Eastern Metropolitan Bypass, Kolkata, West Bengal 700054
blurb: A pure-vegetarian restaurant on the 3rd floor of Mani Square Mall, Kankurgachi, with a broad Asian, Italian and modern-Indian menu.

tips.expect: A well-liked vegetarian dining room that suits families and groups. About ₹1,500 for two.
tips.good: The creative veg menu and the ambience, which many reviewers rate highly.
tips.watch: It is inside a mall, so it is better for a sit-down meal than a quick bite between pandals.
tips.tip: Handy before or after the Maniktala and Phoolbagan pandals.

address: AA 28, 1st Cross Rd, near PNB, AA Block, Sector 1, Bidhannagar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700064
blurb: A popular Salt Lake Sector 1 cafe at AA28, known for coffee, desserts and a good breakfast menu with sourdough.

tips.expect: A relaxed all-day cafe with a long menu: pizza, pasta, sandwiches and a bit of Korean. About ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: Coffee and desserts, and a strong breakfast. It is very well rated.
tips.watch: It's busy at weekends and often has a wait.
tips.tip: A good coffee stop in the Salt Lake blocks cluster (AE, AB, BJ, CE).

address: 19A, Deshapriya Park W, Manoharpukur, Kalighat, Kolkata, West Bengal 700026
Hindustan Rd, Ballygunge, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: A small dessert cafe on Hindustan Road, Ballygunge, known for Middle Eastern-style sweets.

tips.expect: An inexpensive dessert-and-coffee stop. About ₹400 for two, and rated 4.7.
tips.good: The unusual Middle Eastern-style desserts at a low price.
tips.watch: It's tiny, so seats can be hard to find in the evening.
tips.tip: Next door to Amar Khamar on Hindustan Road. A natural sweet finish after dinner.

address: 35, Jagat Banerjee Ghat Rd, near Royal Enfield Showroom, Choura Bustee, Shibpur, Howrah, West Bengal 711102
blurb: A fully vegetarian, tropical-inspired restaurant in Shibpur, Howrah, by chef Prasanta Saha, with lagoon-style outdoor seating and a shisha lounge.

tips.expect: Cafe and fine-dining blended, with reimagined Indian street food. About ₹1,000 for two.
tips.watch: It is across the river in Howrah, so it is not on any pandal circuit.
tips.tip: Only worth the trip if you are on that side of the Ganga.

address: Street Number 372, Action Area I, IIF, Newtown, Kolkata, Chakpachuria, West Bengal 700160
blurb: A beach-themed restaurant in New Town from the Pepper Town group.

tips.expect: A Miami beach look with Asian, Chinese and Italian dishes. About ₹1,000 for two, with veg and non-veg options.
tips.good: The decor, which suits photographs.
tips.watch: It is far out in New Town, away from every pandal circuit on your list.
tips.tip: Only worth it if you are already in New Town or Rajarhat.

Flat no. 22, Ground Floor, Harrington Mansion, 8, Ho Chi Minh Sarani, Kankaria Estates, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071
blurb: A high-energy bar and restaurant in the historic Harrington Mansion on Ho Chi Minh Sarani, with cave-inspired interiors by Akash Roy.

tips.expect: A modern hideout that shifts from a relaxed evening to a nightlife mood. About ₹2,000 for two.
tips.good: The dark, sculptural interior and the mixed Italian, North Indian and Asian menu.
tips.watch: It gets loud later in the evening.
tips.tip: A solid late-night stop close to Park Street.

address: Ambuja Neotia EcoCentre, 20th Floor, EM-4, Street No. 13, EM Block, Sector V, Bidhannagar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700091
blurb: A rooftop restaurant and microbrewery on the 20th and 21st floors of AltAir Boutique Hotel, Sector V, with 360-degree views of the city.

tips.expect: A sky bar with city-skyline views, cocktails and a multicuisine menu. About ₹1,600 for two.
tips.good: The view, which is excellent at night over Salt Lake.
tips.watch: It is high up in an office building: allow time for the lifts and book ahead on weekends.
tips.tip: A strong date-night finish after the Salt Lake pandals.

address: 10/3, Elgin Rd, Sreepally, Bhowanipore, Kolkata, West Bengal 700020
CF-204, Salt Lake Rd, near Sector 1, CF Block, Sector 1, Bidhannagar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700064
7, Sudder St, Fire Brigade Head Quarter, New Market Area, Dharmatala, Taltala, Kolkata, West Bengal 700016
blurb: A small cafe on Sudder Street with indoor and outdoor seating, serving Spanish dishes and wood-fired pizzas.

tips.expect: A tiny, characterful cafe. Reported hours are 8 am to 10 pm.
tips.good: Authentic-style Spanish plates, a rare find in Kolkata, at friendly prices.
tips.watch: It is small and tables are limited at peak times.
tips.tip: Sit outside on Sudder Street and watch the backpacker world go by.

address: 21, Lake Terrace, Lake Market, Kalighat, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
blurb: Eloise Bistro & Boulangerie, a European-style bistro on Lake Terrace with elegant decor and French-leaning food.

tips.expect: A pretty, European-feeling bistro and bakery. Reported hours are noon to 11 pm, and it costs about ₹1,200 or more for two.
tips.good: The signature burrata caprese and the hot chocolate.
tips.watch: It is in the busy Lake Market cafe cluster, so weekends fill up.
tips.tip: Near Deshapriya Park and the Kalighat pandals, so easy to add to a south circuit.

address: 5, Jawaharlal Nehru Rd, Esplanade, Dharmatala, Taltala, Kolkata, West Bengal 700013
blurb: An outlet of the Desi Lane pub chain, which is known for very low-priced drinks.

tips.expect: A busy, no-frills pub and bar-food place. At the Topsia outlet, listings put it at about ₹1,700 for two.
tips.good: Cheap drinks and a lively crowd.
tips.watch: I couldn't confirm details for this exact Esplanade outlet, so prices and hours may differ.
tips.tip: A late-night option near Esplanade after pandal-hopping.

address: DC Block, Sector 1, Bidhannagar, Kolkata, West Bengal 700064
blurb: A Mughlai, Afghan and North Indian restaurant in City Centre 1, Salt Lake.

tips.expect: A family-friendly restaurant with a long kebab, biryani and curry menu. About ₹1,800 for two.
tips.good: The kebabs, especially the Kandahari laham, and the dessert firni.
tips.watch: It is inside a mall, so closing time follows the mall.
tips.tip: Good for dinner after the Salt Lake pandals, as City Centre is on the way back.

blurb: A small coffee bistro, ordering downstairs and seating upstairs, with mocha, Spanish coffee, house brew, espresso and cold brew. About ₹700 for two.

tips.expect: A tiny, cosy coffee spot open about 10 am to 10 pm.
tips.watch: Details are from the chain's listings, and there are separate outlets at Salt Lake and Lake Market.
tips.tip: A quick coffee stop between Sector 1 pandals.

blurb: The Lake Market outlet of the Evabrew coffee bistro.

tips.expect: A small coffee spot with espresso, cold brew and house brew.
tips.tip: A good short coffee break on the Kalighat route.

address: 11/1A, Ho Chi Minh Sarani, opposite Jyoti Vihar, Kankaria Estates, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071
blurb: A vibrant Mexican cantina on Ho Chi Minh Sarani, with murals and a menu of small plates.

tips.expect: A colourful cantina with small plates, tacos, nachos and rice bowls. Tacos are about ₹500 each.
tips.good: A seasonal mango menu, and a rare real Mexican option in Kolkata.
tips.watch: Prices add up quickly if you order several plates and drinks.
tips.tip: Combine with Cove and Sorano in the same building area for a Park Street night.

address: 18A, Park St, Park Street area, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071
139A, Rash Behari Ave, Ballygunge, Kolkata, West Bengal 700029
